extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants and recipients (authorized organization representatives, institutional officials, grant administrators, PIs, and subrecipients)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for identifying and meeting public policy requirements, objectives, and appropriation mandates that apply to NIH grant applications and awards, including animal welfare, civil rights, clinical trials registration, and related statutory/regulatory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and signatures must identify an individual with authority
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not accept forms or other documentation bearing generic departmental signatures or their electronic equivalent (e.g., Department of Sponsored Research). All forms and documentation submitted to NIH must reflect the name of the individual, electronic or otherwise, with the appropriate institutional authority to submit such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signature of the AOR on the application certifies that the organization complies, or intends to comply, with all applicable policies, certifications and assurances referenced in the application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility to monitor compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is responsible for: 1) establishing and maintaining the necessary processes to monitor its compliance and that of its employees, consortium participants, and contractors with these requirements; 2) taking appropriate action to meet the stated objectives; and, 3) informing NIH of any problems or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient should consult award terms and conditions and contact the GMO with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for false or misrepresented information or noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a grant is awarded on the basis of false or misrepresented information, or if a recipient does not comply with these public policy requirements, NIH may take any necessary and appropriate action, including using remedies described in Administrative Requirements—Enforcement Actions or other available legal remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies can include enforcement actions and cost disallowances; recipients should proactively report problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Exhibit 4 to determine applicable public policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit 4 contains information to help the recipient determine what public policy requirements, objectives and appropriations mandates apply to its activities and whether a requirement should be included in a consortium agreement or a contract for routine goods or services under the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exhibit indicates (by 'Y' or 'NA') whether a given requirement normally would apply but should be used only as general guidance since applicability can vary by specific situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to foreign direct recipients and collaborative international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign direct recipients or those under a collaborative international award structure must follow the recipient requirements in Exhibit 4, except when noted as not applicable to foreign awards, awards under a collaborative international award structure nor foreign component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional guidance on applicability to foreign awards is covered in NIHGPS Chapter 16.4; consult the award and GMO for specific applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Welfare Requirements (PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS Policy requires that an approved Animal Welfare Assurance be on file with OLAW at the time of award for all organizations involved in PHS-conducted or supported activities involving live vertebrate animals. Recipients must establish appropriate policies and procedures to ensure humane care and use of animals and bear ultimate responsibility for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHS Policy incorporates U.S. Government Principles and requires programs based on the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; states/locals laws with more stringent standards also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'animal' for PHS Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHS Policy defines 'animal' as any live, vertebrate animal used or intended for use in research, research training, experimentation, biological testing or related purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that propose use of animals must thoroughly address vertebrate animal use in the Research Plan or explain if unknown at time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Welfare Assurance requirement and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: An Animal Welfare Assurance is the document submitted by an institution assuring institutional compliance with the PHS Policy; OLAW requests, negotiates, approves/disapproves, and may restrict or withdraw approval of Assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an applicant institution does not have an Assurance, the AOR's signature constitutes declaration that the institution will submit an Assurance when requested by OLAW; generally an approved Assurance must be on file for award to be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interinstitutional Assurance for performance sites
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pass-through entity does not have an approved Domestic or Foreign Assurance and the animal activities will be conducted at an Assured institution named as a performance site, the recipient must obtain an Interinstitutional Assurance from OLAW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Interinstitutional Assurance, the recipient and performance site agree that the research will be conducted under the program of the performance site's Assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC requirement and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: An Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), appointed by the Chief Executive Officer or designee, is federally mandated to oversee the organization’s animal program, facilities, and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IACUC must review components of the application related to care and use of animals; institutions should ensure appropriate membership and review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of IACUC approval prior to award
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will delay an award for research involving live vertebrate animals until the recipient organization and all performance sites are operating in accordance with approved Animal Welfare Assurances and the recipient has provided verification of IACUC approval of those sections of the application that involve use of vertebrate animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IACUC approval must have been granted not more than three years prior to the budget period start date to be valid; verification may be filed through Just-in-Time unless required earlier by the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: No costs or activities for live vertebrate animals without valid Assurance and IACUC approval
rubrics_metrics.description: No activities with live vertebrate animals may begin and no costs for activities with live vertebrate animals may be charged to NIH if there is not a valid Animal Welfare Assurance and IACUC approval of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges to NIH awards for animal activities during periods where terms and conditions are not upheld are unallowable and will be subject to cost disallowance; NIH may allow maintenance/care costs on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement restrictions for cats and dogs
rubrics_metrics.description: Noncompeting and competing awards are prohibited from using NIH funds to procure cats from USDA Class B dealers; procurement may only be from USDA Class A dealers or other approved legal sources. NIH funds may not be used to procure or support the use of dogs from Class B dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any costs incurred in violation of this policy are unallowable and subject to cost disallowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient accountability for consortium participants' animal welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Under consortium (subaward) agreements, the recipient, as the direct and primary recipient of NIH grant funds, is accountable for the performance of the project, the appropriate expenditure of grant funds by all parties, and all other obligations of the recipient as specified in the NIHGPS. Animal welfare requirements that apply to recipients also apply to consortium participants and subprojects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary recipient must include these requirements in agreements with collaborators and ensure all sites have approved Assurances and valid IACUC approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign recipients and foreign performance sites animal assurance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign recipients that will perform live, vertebrate animal activity onsite must provide OLAW with an Animal Welfare Assurance for Foreign Institutions. This constitutes institutional assurance and certification of compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and policies of the jurisdiction and a commitment to follow International Guiding Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IACUC approval is not required of foreign recipients, but OLAW encourages standards in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements to OLAW
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting requirements under the PHS Policy include an annual report to OLAW describing any change in the institution's program for animal care and use as described in the Assurance, changes in IACUC membership, and the dates the IACUC conducted its semiannual evaluations. The IACUC must promptly report serious or continuing noncompliance, serious deviations, and any IACUC suspensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instances of serious noncompliance are to be reported to OLAW and the IC supporting the grant award; reports must include certifications regarding unallowable costs or detailed accounting if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs unallowable when animal activities occur during noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to NIH grant awards for the conduct of live vertebrate animal activities during periods when the terms and conditions of the grant award are not upheld are not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific unallowable situations include: (1) conduct of animal activities in absence of a valid Animal Welfare Assurance on file with OLAW; (2) conduct in absence of valid IACUC approval (including expiration or suspension). Appropriate adjustments must be made to remove such charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Rights Protections—general compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to administer NIH-funded projects in compliance with federal civil rights laws that prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, disability, age, and sex (including pregnancy), and comply with applicable conscience protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before NIH may make an award to a domestic organization, the AOR must certify that the organization has on file with HHS OCR a one-time Assurance of Compliance (HHS Form 690).

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS Form 690 Assurance of Compliance filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before NIH may make an award to a domestic organization, the AOR must certify, by signature on the application, that the organization has on file with the HHS OCR a one-time Assurance of Compliance with the civil rights statutes described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant recommended for funding does not have an Assurance on file, the awarding IC will provide the required form and instructions; domestic organizations receiving funding from recipients (subrecipients/contractors) are also required to file HHS 690.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title VI—Civil Rights Act of 1964 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title VI provides that no person in the United States shall, on the grounds of race, color, or national origin, be excluded from participation in, denied benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance (HHS implementing regs at 45 CFR Part 80).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure programs and services funded by NIH do not discriminate on Title VI grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX—Education Amendments of 1972 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX provides that no person in the United States shall, on the basis of sex, be excluded from participation in, denied benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any educational program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance (HHS implementing regs at 45 CFR Part 86).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to educational programs/activities funded by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehabilitation Act Section 504 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 504 provides that no otherwise qualified handicapped individual shall, solely by reason of physical or mental impairment, be excluded from participation in, denied benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance (HHS regs at 45 CFR Parts 84 and 85).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements pertain to provision of benefits/services and employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age Discrimination Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Age Discrimination Act of 1975 prohibits discrimination on the basis of age in any program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance (HHS regs at 45 CFR Part 91).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must not discriminate based on age in NIH-funded programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS provides guidance on the obligations of recipients to provide meaningful access to health and social services on the LEP page of the HHS website. A program of language assistance should provide for effective communication between the service provider and the person with limited English proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must take steps to ensure meaningful access and effective communication (including persons with disabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs or Activities (ACA Section 1557)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 of the ACA prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, and disability in certain health programs and activities receiving Federal financial assistance, including NIH-funded programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS implementing regulations codified at 45 CFR Part 92 apply; recipients should review applicability to their health programs/activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Policy on Dissemination of NIH-Funded Clinical Trial Information (ClinicalTrials.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: For grant applications that request support for the conduct of a clinical trial, NIH expects that all NIH-funded recipients and investigators conducting clinical trials will ensure their clinical trials are registered at, and that summary results information is submitted to, ClinicalTrials.gov for public posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy promotes broad and responsible dissemination and is complementary to the regulation at 42 CFR Part 11; applicants seeking NIH funding for clinical trials must submit a plan addressing how expectations will be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: policy applies to all NIH-funded clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy applies to all NIH-funded clinical trials regardless of study phase, type of intervention, or whether they are subject to the regulation (e.g., includes phase 1 trials and trials of non-FDA-regulated interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All NIH-funded trials are expected to register and submit results according to regulation timelines; trials using NIH infrastructure but not NIH funds are not covered by this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Experimental Studies in Humans (BESH) exclusion (effective May 25, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective May 25, 2026, Basic Experimental Studies in Humans (BESH) are no longer considered clinical trials by the NIH; BESH must follow other applicable clinical research laws, regulations, and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BESH must still comply with human subjects protections and NIH Data Management and Sharing Policy as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants must submit a clinical trial information dissemination plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking NIH funding for clinical trials will be required to submit a plan that will address how the expectations of this policy (registration and results submission) will be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and investigators are required to comply with award terms and follow their submitted dissemination plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR certification for clinical trial dissemination compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature of the AOR on the grant application or progress report certifies that, for any clinical trials funded under the NIH award, the recipient and all investigators are in compliance with the recipient’s clinical trial information dissemination plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOR signature also certifies regulatory compliance for applicable clinical trials where recipient is responsible party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities for registration and results (three categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities of recipients and investigators fall within one of three categories: (1) if the NIH-funded trial is an applicable clinical trial under the regulation and the recipient is the responsible party, the recipient ensures regulatory requirements are met; (2) if the trial is an applicable clinical trial but the recipient is not the responsible party, the recipient coordinates with the responsible party; (3) if the trial is not an applicable clinical trial under the regulation, the recipient is responsible for registering and submitting results as described in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must determine their role and ensure tasks/timelines (e.g., registration, results submission) are met accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of IRB-approved consent form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of NIH funding conducting non-exempt research involving human subjects and a clinical trial as defined in 45 CFR Part 46.102(b) should be aware that one IRB-approved consent form must be posted on a designated public federal website after recruitment closes and no later than 60 days after the last study visit by any subject, as required by 45 CFR Part 46.116(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information available on the Posting Clinical Trial Informed Consent Forms webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for submitting informed consent forms (English and non-English)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-funded recipients using an English-language informed consent form may submit an IRB-approved English-language form to ClinicalTrials.gov or submit to Regulations.gov. Recipients using only non-English informed consent forms must submit an IRB-approved form to Regulations.gov (Docket ID provided) per OHRP guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients submitting to Regulations.gov must keep receipt/tracking numbers and protect participant privacy per applicable laws and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect participant privacy when submitting trial documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions submitting documents to either ClinicalTrials.gov or Regulations.gov must protect participant privacy in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations (e.g., HIPAA Privacy Rule, Certificates of Confidentiality) and any applicable terms of their NIH award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure de-identification and compliance with award-specific privacy commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single ClinicalTrials.gov record per NIH-funded clinical trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Each NIH-funded clinical trial should have only one entry in ClinicalTrials.gov that contains its registration and results information; recipients need not and should not create a separate record to comply with this policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid duplicate records; use the existing applicable clinical trial record for registration and results submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDAAA (42 U.S.C. 282(j)) and 42 CFR Part 11 registration/results requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and recipients should familiarize themselves with FDAAA (Sec. 801 of Public Law 110-85) as implemented by 42 CFR Part 11 concerning registration and results information submission requirements that apply to certain clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, results information of applicable clinical trials are due not later than 12 months after the primary completion date; if this date is after the period of performance, results submission is still required in accordance with FDAAA and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature certification for applicable clinical trials under FDAAA
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature of the AOR on the grant or progress report form certifies that, for applicable clinical trials funded in whole or part by the award, the responsible party has made all registration and results submissions required by 42 CFR Part 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure responsible party has met regulatory submissions; AOR signature binds the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Cause Extension (GCE) request eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A good cause extension (GCE) request may be sought in rare instances for certain categories of Applicable Clinical Trials (ACTs) subject to the Final Rule (42 CFR 11.42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCEs are exceptional; applicants/recipients should consult the regulation and IC guidance when considering a GCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients should consult award terms, GMO, and counsel for applicability questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient should consult the terms and conditions of its award and should contact the GMO if it has any question concerning the applicability of a particular public policy requirement or objective. The recipient should also consult its attorney, as appropriate, regarding particular questions about the governing statute or regulation as applied to its specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit 4 and cited policies may provide additional information but are general guidance only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 4 Y/NA designation is general guidance only
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit 4 distinguishes transaction types under a grant and indicates (by 'Y' for Yes or 'NA' for Not Applicable) whether a given requirement normally would apply, but even if the exhibit indicates a requirement is not applicable that requirement potentially could be applicable in a specific situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must evaluate applicability in context (e.g., a contract under a grant that involves research activity may trigger requirements listed as NA by default).
